falsification.text: If variants in CLCN5 and SCNN1A are found to regulate entirely independent cellular processes with no shared downstream effects on epithelial function or ion balance, this hypothesis would be falsified. **Proposed mechanism:** CLCN5 (HGNC:2360) —DISRUPTS→ Renal tubular acidosis (HP:0000111); CLCN5 (HGNC:2360) —DISRUPTS→ Nephrolithiasis (HP:0000119); SCNN1A (HGNC:10610) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) activity (R-HSA-1908905); Epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) activity (R-HSA-1908905) —INCREASES→ Hypertension (HP:0000827); Epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) activity (R-HSA-1908905) —INCREASES→ Hypokalemic alkalosis (HP:0002829); SCNN1A (HGNC:10610) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertension (HP:0000827); SCNN1A (HGNC:10610) —LEADS_TO→ Hypokalemic alkalosis (HP:0002829). Loss-of-function mutations in CLCN5 disrupt renal tubular function, leading to Dent disease phenotypes like nephrolithiasis and renal tubular acidosis. Gain-of-function mutations in SCNN1A lead to overactive epithelial sodium channels (ENaC), causing increased sodium reabsorption and subsequent hypertension and hypokalemic alkalosis, characteristic of Liddle syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in SCNN1A are found to cause Dent disease type 1 phenotypes or if pathogenic variants in CLCN5 are found to cause Liddle syndrome phenotypes with typical electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemic alkalosis), this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: gnomAD analysis revealing high-frequency pathogenic variants in CLCN5 associated with Liddle syndrome or SCNN1A with Dent disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct functional consequences of mutations in CLCN5 and SCNN1A on renal ion transport can inform targeted therapeutic strategies for both Dent disease and Liddle syndrome, potentially involving ion channel modulators or agents that restore electrolyte balance.
